answer: No. Besides the tweets themselves, the paper uses graph/community structure: they combine embeddings built on the user-to-user mention graph, the user-to-hashtag mention graph, and the text of the tweets [11]. More generally, they leverage the community structure of the trolls' social network represented as a graph, from which they extract several types of representations for the trolls [8][3]. Note that they chose node2vec because they lack user attributes (the accounts are suspended), so tweets are the primary content data [1].
